fx_note: BIT.NZ is a thin secondary NZX listing (NZD-quoted) of a UK primary-listed, GBP-reporting closed-end investment trust (LSE: BNKR). All fundamental data (NAV, dividends, discount history) is GBP/pence. current_price and all intrinsic_value/entry_price fields are reported in NZD (to match the NZX quote the user tracks) by converting the GBP-derived valuation at the live GBPNZD rate. A parallel 'gbp' sub-object under each block gives the native pence figures for direct comparison against BNKR.L. Cross-check at valuation date: BNKR.L 152.2p x GBPNZD 2.2888 = NZD 3.4836 vs the actual NZX quote of NZD 3.52, a 1.05% NZX premium - the arbitrage is tight and the NZX quote is judged fair/liquid enough to use directly rather than a synthetic cross-rate price. NZ holders receive NO imputation/franking credits on UK-sourced dividends (UK has no such system for NZ residents) and bear fully unhedged GBP/NZD translation risk stacked on top of the trust's own multi-currency (USD/JPY/EUR) portfolio exposure; NZ FIF/FDR tax rules likely apply for most retail holders, a further drag on the practical dividend-growth thesis not modelled here.
valuation_philosophy: The Bankers Investment Trust is a 138-year-old UK closed-end investment trust (not an operating business): it holds a ~GBP1.4bn globally diversified portfolio of ~80 listed equities, earns dividend/investment income, and distributes a progressive dividend funded by income plus revenue reserves. A standard FCF/WACC/Gordon-growth DCF is INAPPLICABLE - reported operating cash flow is a portfolio-turnover artefact, there is no capex, no SBC, no working-capital cycle, and NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio revaluation (FY2022 -GBP179m, FY2021 +GBP331m). This model instead uses the NAV-compounding + exit-discount framework applied consistently across the LIC/investment-trust names in this research folder (AFI.NZ, FIH.U, FRFHF): (1) project NAV per share (debt-at-fair-value basis, the trust's own headline KPI) forward using a total-return assumption net of the trust's demonstrated ~1.2-4.3pp/yr benchmark underperformance and its 0.51% OCR, split between NAV price growth and the dividend payout; (2) apply a scenario exit discount/premium to that NAV, since the market-clearing valuation metric for an investment trust is its price/NAV discount, not an earnings multiple; (3) headline intrinsic value = TODAY's NAV per share x (1 + scenario fair discount) - i.e. what a rational buyer should pay for today's known NAV at a fair (rather than currently transient near-zero) discount; (4) a separate 5-year IRR build (PV of interim dividends + PV of year-5 exit value at cost of equity) is shown as a cross-check/memo capturing NAV compounding over the horizon. THE CENTRAL VALUATION ISSUE: the trust's discount to NAV has closed from an 8-year average of 7.3% (5-year average 10.6%) to approximately ZERO today (BNKR.L 152.2p vs the last published 30-Apr-2026 NAV of 152.0p), driven by an aggressive buyback programme (GBP185.5m/153.6m shares in FY2025 alone, ~13.4% of shares retired) and a strategy-consolidation narrative. That re-rating has ALREADY HAPPENED - a large share of the trailing-year 30.6% share price total return came from discount narrowing (NAV TR was only 27.6%), not NAV growth, and cannot mechanically repeat. The base case therefore assumes a mild reversion WIDER toward the long-run average discount, not further re-rating, which correctly produces near-zero or negative base-case upside for an asset currently priced at par.

inputs.nav_asof: 2026-04-30 (H1 FY2026 half-year report, released 2026-06-23) - no more current published NAV available
inputs.nav_debt_basis_note: Two NAV bases are published because the GBP124.6m unsecured loan notes are carried at par (book value) on the balance sheet but had an estimated FAIR VALUE of only ~GBP88.5m at 30-Apr-2026 (the notes are deep out-of-the-money at current market rates). NAV-with-debt-at-fair-value (152.0p) therefore EXCEEDS NAV-at-par (148.1p) by ~3.9p/share - a genuine, disclosed valuation difference, not an error. This model uses the debt-at-fair-value basis (152.0p) as primary because it is the Company's own headline KPI and the basis on which its published discount is calculated; a lower economic debt burden (fair value) means a higher true NAV attributable to equity.
inputs.nav_estimate_methodology: The last published NAV is 30-Apr-2026 (152.0p). No more current figure is disclosed. As a transparency exercise only, this rolls the NAV forward using the MSCI World Index (URTH, USD) total return of +8.56% from 30-Apr-2026 to 7-Aug-2026, applying a 90% capture ratio (reflecting the trust's ~5% gearing partially offset by its demonstrated multi-year benchmark underperformance and portfolio composition differences, plus GBP-reporting vs USD-index currency basis mismatch not corrected for). This yields an ESTIMATED current NAV of approximately 163.7p - meaningfully above the 152.0p last-published figure and would put BNKR.L's 152.2p share price at an estimated ~7% discount to an UNPUBLISHED, model-estimated NAV. This estimate is presented for context only and is NOT used in the valuation below, which anchors strictly to the last published, audited/board-reported NAV (152.0p) to avoid compounding estimation error into a headline output.
inputs.dividend_track_record: 59 consecutive years of dividend growth (AIC 'Dividend Hero'), 60th year pending FY2026 (Board guiding at least 3% growth, implying >=2.826p)
inputs.revenue_reserve_cover_note: Revenue reserves of ~2.44p/share cover only ~0.9x the current annual dividend (2.744p) - the 59-year streak is partly reserve-funded as portfolio income declines with the rotation toward lower-yielding US technology names (H1 FY2026 net revenue fell to GBP10.0m from GBP12.6m). This is a genuine, disclosed sustainability caveat on the dividend-growth element of the thesis.
inputs.units: millions except per-share figures (pence) and NAV/price data
inputs.sbc_note: Not applicable - Bankers is an externally-managed investment trust (Janus Henderson); no stock-based compensation, dilution mechanic, capex or working-capital cycle exists in this model.
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable - see valuation_philosophy. No FCF projection, WACC-Gordon terminal value, or SBC adjustment is used; those schema fields below are populated with null plus explanatory notes for schema consistency with operating-company DCFs, and are replaced functionally by the NAV-compounding equivalents.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable - not applicable to an externally-managed investment trust; see fcf_dcf_note
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2025 share repurchases (GBP183.388m per kpis table; disclosed as GBP185.5m in the Annual Report inclusive of costs) plus GBP76.429m in H1 FY2026 - real cash outflow in financing activities, not merely an authorization. Buybacks reduce share count and are NAV-accretive when executed below NAV, but do not offset any 'dilution' concept since this is not an SBC-driven business.
inputs.projected_shares_note: Held flat for projection purposes. Buybacks are modelled as NAV-accretive (embedded in the total-return assumption) rather than as a separate share-count mechanic, since (unlike an SBC-diluting operating company) there is no offsetting dilution to net against.
inputs.currency_note: Fundamentals (NAV, income, net assets) are GBP; valuation outputs (intrinsic_value, entry_price) are reported in NZD to match the BIT.NZ quote, converted at GBPNZD 2.2888. Native pence figures are in the "gbp" sub-object. Previously: "GBP (fundamentals) / NZD (reported valuation outputs)".

historical_growth.methodology: Bankers' own preferred value driver is NAV-per-share TOTAL RETURN (NAV growth + dividends paid), disclosed against the FTSE World Index benchmark. Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs are shown below for schema completeness but are NOT the growth driver used in projections - NetIncome/EPS for a trust is dominated by unrealised/realised capital gains timing (FY2021 +GBP330.6m, FY2022 -GBP179.2m) rather than an operating trend, and 'Revenue' is investment income only (declining structurally as the portfolio rotates from income/value names into lower-yielding growth/technology names).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nav_total_return_base_case_assumption (not a pure historical CAGR - see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR is not meaningful for this ticker (NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings, e.g. FY2021 EPS 0.253 vs FY2022 EPS -0.137 on the same order of magnitude of shares) and is left null rather than computed. Equity (net assets) CAGR is depressed versus NAV-per-share growth because the FY2025 buyback programme shrank the share count materially (992.3m at FY2025-end vs 1,145.9m at FY2024-end) while returning capital - net assets grew slower than NAV-per-share by design.
historical_growth.notes: The defining historical fact for this ticker is PERSISTENT NAV total-return underperformance versus the FTSE World Index: -1.2pp/yr over 10 years, -4.3pp/yr over 5 years, -5.0pp/yr over 3 years (driven by the historic four-region 'sleeve' structure and a value/income tilt that missed the US mega-cap tech rally). The base-case 7.0% total-return assumption is built as a long-run global-equity nominal return expectation (~8.5-9%) minus a persisting-but-partially-narrowing structural drag (the sleeve structure was unified and US/tech weighting raised from 50% to 67% between late 2024 and Apr-2026, but the new lead manager, Richard Clode, has under 18 months' track record at Bankers and does not take sole control until Dec-2026) minus the 0.51% OCR. This is meaningfully below the exceptional trailing 1yr NAV TR of 27.6%, which reflects a strong global equity bull market and should NOT be extrapolated.

base.rationale: Long-run global equity total return (~8.5-9%) net of Bankers' demonstrated multi-year benchmark underperformance (only partially assumed to narrow, given the unified-portfolio strategy is unproven and the new lead manager's sole tenure has not yet begun) and the 0.51% OCR. Exit discount reverts toward the 8-year historical average (-7.3%) blended slightly toward the wider 5-year average (-10.6%), reflecting the view that today's near-zero discount is a transient, buyback- and sentiment-driven condition that is unlikely to persist for a trust with this performance history, rather than a new sustainable equilibrium. This produces modest NEGATIVE base-case upside - the correct, honest output for an asset currently priced at essentially par to NAV.

bull.rationale: The unified ~60-80 stock portfolio under Richard Clode succeeds in closing the performance gap (broadening market leadership beyond mega-cap tech plays to Bankers' historically diversified strength), NAV total return converges toward the benchmark, and the Board's continued aggressive discount-control buybacks plus improved sentiment hold the discount near par (consistent with where it trades today).

bear.rationale: Underperformance persists or worsens as the AI/mega-cap-tech concentration (Technology now 36.9% of the portfolio, US weight 67%) becomes a new source of drawdown risk rather than a fix (per the Feb-Mar 2026 'AI disruption'/SaaSpocalypse selloff already seen in H1 FY2026), global equities de-rate from current all-time highs, ~5% gearing amplifies the NAV drawdown, and the discount reverts to its FY2023 wide of -15.8% (close to the -14% used here) as investor confidence in the strategy fades again.

five_year_irr_build_memo.description: Cross-check to the headline 'current NAV x fair discount' intrinsic value: PV of the 5-year dividend stream plus PV of the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x scenario exit discount), both discounted at the scenario's cost of equity. This captures compounding of NAV growth over the horizon that the simpler current-NAV framing does not.

base.terminal_pct_of_value: n/a - not an FCF DCF; see five_year_irr_build_memo (exit value is ~89% of the 5yr-build fair value)
base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - trust valuation uses P/NAV, not an earnings multiple

entry_price.methodology: Price today such that 5 years of projected base-case dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x base-case -8.5% exit discount) discounted at 15% equals that price. Uses base-case cashflows only (per dcf-analyst methodology).
entry_price.memo: A 15% IRR hurdle applied to an asset whose base-case total return is only ~7% p.a. mechanically requires buying at an extremely deep discount to today's NAV (~-34.6%, versus Bankers' own observed 8-year discount range of roughly -0.4% to -15.8%). This is DEEPER than Bankers has ever traded in the available history, so this is NOT an achievable near-term entry target - it should be read as 'this ticker cannot organically deliver a 15% forward IRR at any price it has historically reached' rather than as a realistic buy level. A diversified, geared global-equity investment trust with a ~7-9% expected total return should instead be judged against its cost of equity (~9%), not a 15% private-equity-style hurdle. On that basis, buying today at NZD 3.52 (GBp 152.2, essentially at par to the last published NAV) offers a prospective 5-year return of roughly the base-case ~7% total return LESS a modest discount-widening drag (base case implies -8.62% price return over 5 years net of the discount reversion, i.e. total return to a holder is total-return-on-NAV minus the cost of the discount closing having already happened) - in short, today's price already embeds close to the trust's own long-run NAV compounding rate with none of the historical discount cushion left.

sanity_check.description: For an investment trust the natural sanity anchor is price/NAV (P/NAV), not P/E or EV/EBITDA - both are set to null below because reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (FY2022 -GBP179.2m, FY2021 +GBP330.6m) and there is no EBITDA concept for a portfolio of listed securities. The check trips if an implied scenario P/NAV is narrower (more of a premium) than the trust's own best-ever historical discount (-0.4% in FY2020, i.e. essentially at par) - none of the three scenarios below breach that, so the check passes by construction, though the CURRENT market price itself is right at the edge of the historical range (see note).

implied_multiples.price_to_earnings: n/a - NetIncome is mark-to-market, not an operating earnings concept
implied_multiples.ev_to_ebitda: n/a - no EBITDA concept for a listed-securities portfolio

historical_averages_ex_outliers.note: No outlier years excluded - all 8 years (FY2018-FY2025) are used as-is since the discount series does not contain data-quality anomalies, only genuine market-driven variation (e.g. the FY2020 near-par reading reflects the COVID-recovery rally, and FY2023's -15.8% wide reflects the 2022-23 UK investment-trust sector de-rating / rate-shock episode, both real market conditions rather than reporting artefacts).

sanity_check.diagnosis: The three DCF scenarios are all constructed directly from the last published NAV per share and are each within (base, bear) or at (bull, effectively priced to a 2% discount) Bankers' own disclosed 8-year P/NAV range of roughly -15.8% to +0.6%, so they pass by construction and do not require a fix. The genuinely notable finding is that TODAY'S ACTUAL MARKET PRICE (approximately +0.13% to NAV, i.e. essentially at par) sits at the extreme narrow (premium) end of that historical range, alongside only the FY2020 COVID-rally reading. A trust that has averaged a 7.3% discount over 8 years and 10.6% over 5 years is currently priced as if that discount has permanently disappeared, which the base case explicitly does not assume will persist.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required - no scenario breaches the historical range. This model is dated 2026-08-09, after the 2026-07-21 entry-price formula fix (interim cashflows + terminal value at the hurdle rate, not terminal value alone); the entry_price block above uses the corrected formula.

sensitivity.methodology: 5-year IRR-build fair value (PV of dividends + PV of exit value at year-5 NAV x row exit discount, both discounted at the 9.0% base-case cost of equity) in GBP pence, converted to NZD at 2.2888.

probability_weighted.weighted_iv_currency_note: weighted_iv is stated in NZD to match the BIT.NZ quote currency used by the screener; weighted_iv_gbp_pence is the native London (BNKR.L) figure in pence.

discount_history_pct.note: Values as disclosed by the Company (positive = discount, negative = premium), all on the debt-at-fair-value NAV basis. 8-year average 7.31%; 5-year (FY21-25) average 10.62%; range -0.4% (narrowest, FY2020) to 15.8% (widest, FY2023).
